body.text: Why does Bibliography of China's reform and opening still shape capital allocation and market pricing across global desks? Behind the headline numbers lies a structural mechanism that quietly governs liquidity, risk, and long-term purchasing power.

Bibliography of China's reform and opening is a list of English-language books and scholarly articles on the history of the People's Republic of China from the death of Mao Zedong in 1976 to the eve of the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests.
Works whose coverage extends beyond 1989 are included where they treat this period in substantial detail.

This bibliography contains academic-level English-language books (including translations) and journal articles, published mainly after World War II. Book entries may have references to reviews published in academic journals or major newspapers when these could be considered helpful. These reference reviews also function as a resource to find other works on this subject.

body.text: Works listed here are cited in the notes or bibliographies of scholarly sources. Each is published by an academic or major trade press, written by a recognized expert, or substantially reviewed in scholarly journals, borderline cases are omitted. A selection of primary sources is included.
Many of the books below carry their own bibliographies, see Further reading section for longer ones, and External links section for historical sites and museums.

Books have citations to academic journal or mainstream published reviews when available. For books only partly about the subject, relevant chapter or section titles are given where useful and available. Translators of the original-language edition are included when possible.
In cases where a title or name has appeared with more than one English spelling, the most recent published form is used and a footnote documents any earlier title under which the work appeared.
General surveys

The Deng Xiaoping era: An inquiry into the fate of Chinese socialism, 1978, 1994.
Prestige, manipulation, and coercion: Elite power struggles in the Soviet Union and China after Stalin and Mao.

The case of the Gang of Four: With first translation of Teng Hsiao-ping's "Three poisonous weeds".
Background to the fall of Hua Guofeng. Asian Survey, 22(3), 237, 260.
The dragon and the snake: An American account of the turmoil in China, 1976, 1977.
Hua Kuo-feng and the arrest of the "Gang of Four". The China Quarterly, 75, 540, 565.
Leadership, legitimacy, and conflict in China: From a charismatic Mao to the politics of succession.
The end of the Maoist era: Chinese politics during the twilight of the Cultural Revolution, 1972, 1976.
Political

Politics of disillusionment: The Chinese Communist Party under Deng Xiaoping, 1978, 1989.

Ideology
Chinese Marxism in flux, 1978, 84: Essays on epistemology, ideology, and political economy.
Economic transition and political legitimacy in post-Mao China: Ideology and reform. State University of New York Press.
The Communist Party of China and Marxism, 1921, 1985: A self portrait.
From post-Maoism to post-Marxism: The erosion of official ideology in Deng's China.
Ideology and policy in China since the Third Plenum, 1978, 84. Contemporary China Institute, School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London.
Changes and continuities in Chinese communism: Vol. Ideology, politics, and foreign policy.
Political reform
Hu Yaobang's intellectual network and the Theory Conference of 1979. The China Quarterly, 126, 219, 242.
Sowing the seeds of democracy in China: Political reform in the Deng Xiaoping era.
China's intellectuals and the state: In search of a new relationship. Council on East Asian Studies, Harvard University.
Scientism and humanism: Two cultures in post-Mao China, 1978, 1989. State University of New York Press.
Political reform in post-Mao China: Democracy and bureaucracy in a Leninist state.
Domestic policy
Economic reform
Unlikely partners: Chinese reformers, Western economists, and the making of global China.
China's open door policy: The quest for foreign technology and capital. University of British Columbia Press.
Inflation and investment controls in China: The political economy of central-local relations during the reform era.
The Chinese economy: Structure and reform in the domestic economy and in foreign trade.
Chinese firms and the state in transition: Property rights and agency problems in the reform era.
The economic transformation of South China: Reform and development in the post-Mao era. East Asia Program, Cornell University.
Learning from Shenzhen: China's post-Mao experiment from special zone to model city.
The special economic zones of China and their impact on its economic development.
Joint ventures in the People's Republic of China: The control of foreign direct investment under socialism.
The political economy of reform in post-Mao China. Council on East Asian Studies, Harvard University.
How China opened its door: The political success of the PRC's foreign trade and investment reforms.
From lathes to looms: China's industrial policy in comparative perspective, 1979, 1982.
Rural reform
Remaking peasant China: Problems of rural development and institutions at the start of the 1990s.
The spiral road: Change in a Chinese village through the eyes of a Communist Party leader.
Continuity and change in China's rural development: Collective and reform eras in perspective.
Calamity and reform in China: State, rural society, and institutional change since the Great Leap Famine.
Rural reform and peasant income in China: The impact of China's post-Mao rural reforms in selected regions.
Law
To steal a book is an elegant offense: Intellectual property law in Chinese civilization.
Labor dispute resolution in China: Implications for labor rights and legal reform. Institute of East Asian Studies, University of California, Berkeley.
Criminal justice in post-Mao China: Analysis and documents. State University of New York Press.
Anti-crime campaigns and Chinese criminal justice, 1979, 1985. East Asia Program, Cornell University.
The politics of lawmaking in post-Mao China: Institutions, processes, and democratic prospects.
Population policy
China's hidden children: Abandonment, adoption, and the human costs of the one-child policy.
Environment
Patterns of China's lost harmony: A survey of the country's environmental degradation and protection.
Energizing China: Reconciling environmental protection and economic growth. Harvard University Committee on Environment.
Health and medicine
Social origins of distress and disease: Depression, neurasthenia, and pain in modern China.
Mental health planning for one billion people: A Chinese perspective. University of British Columbia Press.
Mental health care in China: State policies, professional services and family responsibilities.
Traditional medicine in contemporary China. Center for Chinese Studies, University of Michigan.
Society
Work and inequality in urban China. State University of New York Press.
Urban spaces in contemporary China: The potential for autonomy and community in post-Mao China.
The return of the god of wealth: The transition to a market economy in urban China.
Mao's children in the new China: Voices from the Red Guard generation.
Contesting citizenship in urban China: Peasant migrants, the state, and the logic of the market.
The flow of gifts: Reciprocity and social networks in a Chinese village.
Education
China's universities: Post-Mao enrollment policies and their impact on the structure of secondary education. Center for Chinese Studies, University of Michigan.
China's education reform in the 1980s: Policies, issues, and historical perspectives. Institute of East Asian Studies, University of California, Berkeley.
Radicalism and education reform in 20th-century China: The search for an ideal development model.
China's brain drain to the United States: Views of overseas Chinese students and scholars in the 1990s. Institute of East Asian Studies, University of California, Berkeley.
Labor and workers
Trade unions in China, 1949 to the present: The organization and leadership of the All-China Federation of Trade Unions.
Smashing the iron rice pot: Workers and unions in China's market socialism.
Women and gender
Changing identities of Chinese women: Rhetoric, experience, and self-perception in twentieth-century China.
Women and sexuality in China: Dominant discourses of female sexuality and gender since 1949.
